Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9); a role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks (set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- Kitsune: a Kitsune with no swallowed attack who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) laid a fox charm on its target. Resolve the charm FIRST, before any other protection (Medic, Trapper, ...): use the kitsune_charm op with every non-Divine Attack on the charmed player tonight, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced, e.g. 'Katana', 'Serial Killer')}, [] if none. Code picks the one the charm swallows and says which: treat it as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), then resolve the other attacks normally. Several charms on one player: one kitsune_charm op each, every one listing all the attacks; code has them act in random order, each swallowing a different attack. A Kitsune holding a swallowed attack can't charm; if it acted with a target (and wasn't role-blocked), use the kitsune_release op: code says the attack's level and cause, and you resolve it like any attack by the Kitsune on that target (a visit). If it kills, kill with exactly that cause, by the Kitsune, katana false; a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Kitsune. Code tells the Kitsune its results; don't tell() it about the charm or the release.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.
